But last quarter's revenue beat and raise bought -0.55% and then a -5.6% drift on a margin cut, the EPS bar of $0.08 asks for a sequential margin recovery that is not guaranteed, and peers' relief rallies (ACN, EPAM) are partly in the +6.8% 5-day run-up. p_up 55 on abs 5.5 gives +0.55; the findings sum to +0.85 because each is sized alone and the revenue-side items are not what this name pays for.

findings.finding: Q3 2026 USD/BRL averaged about 5.145 (July 5.131, August 5.159, September 5.144, monthly means of daily mids). The Q3 revenue guide of at least $145.7m assumed 5.17, so a stronger real gives a small translation tailwind on the roughly 50% of revenue booked in Latin America ($72.0m of $142.8m in 2Q26). In Q2 CI&T guided at least $140.0m at 5.11, the real averaged about 5.06, and it printed $142.8m (+2.0% over the floor). A similar clearance puts Q3 at about $147-149m against the $146.6m consensus, a beat of roughly 0.5-1.5%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Confirmed earnings 6-Ks (EDGAR filing list): 2Q26 on 2026-08-11 beat the revenue floor by 2%, raised FY revenue and cut the margin guide, and the stock moved -0.55% and drifted -5.6% afterwards (earningswhispers). Revenue beats have not been paid on this name; the margin is the line. Earlier earnings reactions: +10.9% (2025-08-13), -0.65% (2025-11-12), +2.6% (2026-03-11), -4.3% (2026-05-11).
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus at $146.6m sits only 0.6% above the guide floor, which suggests the street has not marked up for the FX tailwind or for the company's habit of clearing its floor by about 2%. If it had, consensus would sit near $148m. But a revenue beat is the expected outcome on this name, so most of it is priced.
findings.independence: Q2 guide and FX assumption from the 1Q26 6-K https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001868995/000129281426002933/cintfs1q26_6k.htm; Q3 guide and FX assumption from the 2Q26 6-K. Shares the FX series with the margin and November-BRL findings.

findings.finding: The margin guide needs a second-half step-up that the Q3 EPS bar already assumes. H1 2026 adjusted EBITDA was $20.8m (15.2% on $136.6m) plus $19.0m (13.3% on $142.8m), which is 14.25% on $279.4m. Reaching even the 15.0% low end of the FY guide needs about 15.7% in H2. The $0.08 EPS consensus (against $0.07 adjusted in Q2) implies adjusted profit of about $10.4m, an adjusted EBITDA margin of roughly 14.5-15% in Q3. Year on year the margin will fall sharply from 18.5% in 3Q25, with the real about 5.5% stronger than 3Q25's 5.447 average. A Q3 below about 14.5% would put the low end of the FY margin guide in doubt again.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The margin line is what sold this stock: the 2Q26 margin miss and guide cut (17-19% to 15-17%) on 2026-08-11 was followed by a -5.6% post-earnings drift and a slide to about $3; the 1Q26 print on 2026-05-11 moved -4.3%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the stock is -40% from its high and consensus EPS was cut. What is not visible is whether the sequential recovery starts in Q3. The FX-neutral 2Q26 margin was 15.6% and the real weakened about 1.7% from Q2 to Q3 (worth roughly +35bp by the company's own Q2 FX-neutral bridge). But sales expense ran at 12% of revenue against about 8% a year earlier, and management called that deliberate. If the market were sure of the recovery, the stock would not sit near its 200-day moving average discount (about $3.95 per earningswhispers).
findings.independence: Q3 2025 margin of 18.5% from https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1868995/000129281425003930/cintfs3q25_6k.htm; consensus EPS from finviz 2026-11-03 and earningswhispers. Same 6-K as the revenue finding, different line.

findings.finding: The Brazilian real weakened to about 5.45-5.50 per dollar in early November 2026, after Lula's re-election and the BCB's Selic hold at 13.75%. The November-to-date mean is 5.499, against the 5.17 the company used for its full-year guide, so the real is about 6% weaker than assumed. CI&T's cost base is mostly Brazilian payroll and it has no FX hedging program (2Q26 6-K). The company's own Q2 bridge put about 230bp of margin on an approximately 11% year-on-year BRL appreciation (13.3% reported against 15.6% FX-neutral), which implies about +120bp of Q4 margin tailwind if the real holds. That makes the 15-17% FY margin guide easier to defend when the Q4 outlook is given tonight. It also cuts Q4 USD revenue by roughly 2.5-3% through translation, so the headline revenue guide could be trimmed while constant-currency growth holds.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The FX-driven margin guide cut in August (stronger real) was followed by -0.55% and a -5.6% drift. A guide move on margin is the line this stock has reacted to. No prior case of a weaker-real margin tailwind was found in the reactions.
findings.why_not_priced: Part of it may be in the +6.8% 5-day run-up. But the same weeks carried an AI-stock sell-off and Brazil risk aversion, and the street's $0.08 Q3 bar is a Q3 number that is unaffected. If the market had fully priced a Q4 margin tailwind on the debated line, consensus FY margin and the stock would have re-rated more than 8% over 20 days, which is no more than the peers' relief rally. It is macro-to-company transmission: the company has quantified the sensitivity but has not said anything about the November level.
findings.independence: FX sensitivity from the company's 2Q26 FX-neutral bridge (https://quartr.com/events/ci-t-cint-q2-2026_F36G8ER2); monthly BRL means from https://www.poundsterlinglive.com/history/USD-BRL-2026. Shares the FX series with the first finding.

findings.finding: Peer read since CI&T last spoke has been positive for IT services. Accenture's FQ4 2026 (released 2026-10-01) beat its guided range at $18.68bn, +7% local currency, and the stock rose about 23% as AI-disruption fears eased. EPAM's Q3 2026 (2026-11-05) beat with 16.7% non-GAAP operating margin, raised its FY growth to 3.5-3.7%, and the stock jumped about 7%. Globant does not report until 2026-11-19.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No measured history of CINT reacting to peer prints; the sector move into the print is reflected in CINT's +6.8% 5-day and +8.2% 20-day run-up.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced through the run-up. What remains is that CI&T grows organically at 14-22% against EPAM's 2-4%, so a demand-environment confirmation supports the revenue guide. It is a proxy, not a company number.
findings.independence: Accenture: https://www.tikr.com/es/blog/accenture-soars-23-as-q4-beat-eases-ai-fears-another-year-of-broad-based-growth (Oct 2026); EPAM stock move: https://dev.ua/en/news/epam-shares-soar-7-after-third-quarter-report-company-adds-800-people (single secondary source).

findings.finding: A buyback authorization for up to 5 million Class A shares runs to 2026-12-31. Only 1,393,236 shares ($6.2m) were bought in H1 2026, against $17.6m in H1 2025. With the stock near $3 through Q3 and Q4, the release may show stepped-up Q3 repurchases or a renewal or extension of the program.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No release isolating a buyback reaction found.
findings.why_not_priced: The program's expiry on 2026-12-31 means a renewal decision is due around this print, and nothing has been announced. Net debt of about $82m limits capacity, which is why this is small.

findings.finding: CI&T joined Anthropic's Claude Partner Network in June 2026 (certifying 1,000+ engineers) and signed a multi-year preferred-partner deal with Mistral for Latin America on 2026-07-15. These are the first full quarter of AI-partnership commentary. 30% of new engagements were already on value-based pricing in 2Q26, which the company credited for gross margin expansion to 32.4%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Announcements in June and July were not followed by a re-rating; the stock slid after the August print.
findings.why_not_priced: Public and old, so mostly priced. The only unpriced part is any quantified AI revenue or bookings number in the release, and nothing points to one.
findings.independence: Mistral partnership: https://securitybrief.co.uk/story/ci-t-mistral-strike-latin-america-ai-partnership (July 2026); value-based pricing share from https://quartr.com/events/ci-t-cint-q2-2026_F36G8ER2

findings.finding: At 2026-06-30 CI&T carried $135.8m of loans, $91.4m of them current, including about $51.4m of FX advances on export contracts (ACCs, working-capital financing typical of a Brazilian exporter of services), against $53.4m of cash. Net debt was about $82m, with covenant net debt/EBITDA at or below 3.0x, in compliance. A refinancing or roll is likely in H2.
findings.why_not_priced: Asked what the money buys: ACCs are working capital against USD export receivables, not distress. Leverage is about 1x LTM adjusted EBITDA (roughly $80m), far inside the 3.0x covenant, so it is signed zero.
